checks: The rectangle has seven equal sampled intervals, symmetric about the true mixed centroid. Its positive slopes have radius min(3,1/|s|), and at level k the one-dimensional fiber change contributes k to the density on |s|≤1/k.

For any compact convex competitor containing zero, the positive chart has area Jacobian r. Its ordinary angular-area density is the squared ray length divided by two, without any relation to the original central fiber.

On the two adjacent positive-density open intervals the required reciprocal radii are unequal constants almost everywhere. The extended convex gauge is finite on full-measure subsets of both intervals; by convexity its one-dimensional restriction has 1/2 in the interior of its domain and is continuous near that point. The discontinuity cannot be removed on a null set.

The closed integer knots are at radii 1, 2 and 3 with arithmetic sums 1, 3 and 6. The convex chord at 1/2 uses weights 1/4 and 3/4. The reversed chord inequality reduces by positive multiplications and squaring to 289>216, checked independently.

The polynomial interpolation gives s(1+s)^(-1/2) on (1/3,1), whose second derivative is exactly −(1+s/4)/(1+s)^(5/2). This is a separate interpolation obstruction, not a constraint imposed by almost-everywhere matching.
Verified the source digest and both source locations in §2. They distinguish the interval obstruction from the exact knots and polynomial rule.

overlap.comparison: Constructs a slope-space measure of low normalized depth in two continuous dimensions. The present one-dimensional positive slope law asks for realization by ambient ordinary angular area of a convex set; failure of that realization is a different conclusion.

readability: No full-dimensionality or interior-origin hypothesis is needed for the hypothetical convex set; positivity on the two slope intervals supplies the necessary finite gauge domain locally.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The rectangle excludes almost-everywhere convex angular-area matching and, separately, convex interpolation at the three arithmetic knots.
